newsitem.title: USA: FAA orders inspection of some Boeing 747 fuel wires.
newsitem.headline: FAA orders inspection of some Boeing 747 fuel wires.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration has ordered an inspection of fuel pump wiring systems in older Boeing 747 jumbo jets to look for chafed wiring that could cause an explosion.
The order is part of the FAA's continued probe into the cause of the explosion that destroyed TWA Flight 800 off Long Island, N.Y., on July 17, killing all 230 people on board.
The FAA confirmed on Saturday that the emergency directive, which they had first indicated on Dec. 13 they intended to issue, would go into effect on Jan 21.
The directive covers the 433 oldest Boeing 747s still in service and gives airlines 120 days to do the inspections and correct problems.

Investigators are looking at whether a fuel-system malfunction could have ignited the explosion that downed the TWA 747. The directive says fuel-system electrical wires, which are bundled inside an aluminum conduit, are susceptible to chafing.

The FAA and Boeing had been aware of the problem since 1979, and a directive was issued at that time requiring that the use of auxiliary fuel tanks be discontinued unless they had been retrofitted with a Teflon sleeve over the wiring.
Even so, the FAA directive says, "Such abrasions, if not corrected, could result in electrical arcing between the wires and the aluminim conduit and subsequent fire or explosion of the fuel tank."
